findings.title: TestLogger.FromContext throws away what it logs, and the new logging path has no tests
findings.body:
`FromContext` returns a fresh `NewTestLogger()`, so nothing logged through it shows up in the receiver's `InfoLogs`/`ErrorLogs`. `LoggerMiddleware.logRequest` now logs only through `m.logger.FromContext(ctx).Info(...)` (logger_middleware.go:58). A test built on `TestLogger` therefore can't check that "Plugin Request Completed" is emitted, or which attributes it has.

This matters more now because `pluginId`, `endpoint`, `uname`, `dsName` and `dsUID` used to be added by `logRequest` itself. They now depend on `NewContextualLoggerMiddleware` sitting before `NewLoggerMiddleware` in `CreateMiddlewares` (pluginsintegration.go:160-161). The PR adds no test that would catch a reordering. Two possible fixes: return `f` from the fake's `FromContext`, or record the context. Then add a test that runs ContextualLoggerMiddleware followed by LoggerMiddleware.

findings.title: Test function still uses the old InstrumentationMiddleware name
findings.body: The PR renames the type to `MetricsMiddleware`/`newMetricsMiddleware`, but the test is still called `TestInstrumentationMiddleware`. Rename it to `TestMetricsMiddleware` to match.

contracts.action: New ContextualLoggerMiddleware adds plugin/request attributes to ctx via log.WithContextualAttributes before calling next
contracts.equivalent_path: Before this PR, InstrumentationMiddleware.instrumentPluginRequest called instrumentContext just before fn(ctx). It ran only after pluginTarget succeeded (metrics_middleware.go:104-113)
contracts.before_after: Same attributes (endpoint, pluginId, dsName, dsUID, uname). They are now added in a separate middleware right after MetricsMiddleware in the chain. If pluginTarget fails, the metrics middleware returns early, so the downstream contextual middleware never runs, which is the same outcome as before
contracts.visible_effect: Downstream loggers that call FromContext pick up these attributes through the ctxLogProvider registered in infra/log init
contracts.failure_mode: No async work. A nil req would panic, but MetricsMiddleware already dereferences req earlier in the chain

contracts.action: LoggerMiddleware logs through m.logger.FromContext(ctx) and no longer adds pluginId, endpoint, uname, dsName, dsUID or traceID itself
contracts.equivalent_path: The removed explicit params. traceID is now supplied by the provider registered in tracing.go
contracts.before_after: ContextualLoggerMiddleware runs first (pluginsintegration.go:160-161), so the attributes are present in ctx. traceID comes from the tracing ctx provider
contracts.visible_effect: The "Plugin Request Completed" log line carries the same keys as before
contracts.failure_mode: If the middleware order changes or the contextual middleware is left out, the attributes disappear without any error. No test covers this

contracts.action: grafanaInfraLogWrapper.FromContext type-asserts the infra logger to *ConcreteLogger
contracts.before_after: ConcreteLogger.FromContext always returns either cl.New(...) or cl, both *ConcreteLogger, so the assertion always succeeds
contracts.failure_mode: The fallback d.New() can't be reached today

summary: This PR splits the contextual-logger enrichment out of the old InstrumentationMiddleware into a new ContextualLoggerMiddleware, renames InstrumentationMiddleware to MetricsMiddleware, and has LoggerMiddleware log through FromContext. I found no defects. The middleware order in CreateMiddlewares feeds the same attributes to the request log, traceID still comes from the tracing provider, and nothing still refers to the old names. Two small findings: the TestLogger fake's FromContext throws away what it logs, so the new logging path can't be tested and there are no tests for it; and the test function still uses the old InstrumentationMiddleware name.
